newsitem.title: USA: U S West jumps after upbeat analyst meeting.
newsitem.headline: U S West jumps after upbeat analyst meeting.

text.p: Shares of U S West Communications Group rallied Friday after the company told Wall Street analysts it expects to see double-digit growth in its core business and bottom-line earnings growth of four-to-six percent in the near term.
U S West gained 1-5/8 to 35-1/2 and was one of the most active issues on the New York Stock Exchange.
At an investor conference held Thursday in New York, U S West said financial trends over the last half of 1996 should continue into 1997.

The Colorado-based telecommunications company said it will use the double-digit growth in its core business to fund certain "growth initiatives," so bottom-line growth will be more moderate, the company said.

U S West said it is poised to post further growth in the core business, sustain cost-cutting initiatives started in mid-1996, and move aggressively into wireless and interLATA long distance. The cost-cutting efforts will save about $1 billion over the next several years, U S West said.
U S West warned analysts, however, that local competition will heat up this year.

"Competition for our local customers will intensify in 1997. Some share loss in certain markets is inevitable," said U S West Chief Executive Sol Trujillo in a prepared statement released after the investor conference.

"Some share loss in certain markets is inevitable. But our local presence and strong brand, our longstanding relationship with customers, and our ability to integrate services will delight our existing customers," Trujillo said.
